greeting.title: Hello
greeting.text: Hello! I am Maya. Let us keep Panjim dry.

tips.title: The red warning
tips.text: See the red? That is where the next storm will hit hardest. It grows redder each season until the day it comes.

tips.title: Mangroves
tips.text: Mangroves slow the surge before it reaches the houses. Plant them on the wetland edge early: they take a few years to grow.

tips.title: Khazans
tips.text: A khazan stores floodwater in its fields, so the homes around it stay dry, every turn.

tips.title: Dunes and pandanus
tips.text: Dunes and sandy vegetation shield the beach. Pandanus roots hold the sand when the wind gets up.

tips.title: Seawalls
tips.text: A seawall helps, but it costs more and does not absorb water. If a storm is bigger than the wall, the wall fails all at once.

tips.title: Green shields
tips.text: The green shields mark what your defences are protecting. Red with no shield is still open.

tips.title: Get ready
tips.text: I keep a short Get ready list for the next storm, bottom right. Every item is optional, and each one pays.

voices.title: Anthony, Miramar
voices.text: Anthony fishes off Miramar. He says the tide takes more beach every year. Two dunes there and his boat has somewhere to land.

voices.title: Mrs Fernandes, Fontainhas
voices.text: Mrs Fernandes says the Ourem creek comes up her lane every monsoon. Mangroves along the creek would slow it down.

voices.title: Sitaram, Taleigao
voices.text: Sitaram farms in Taleigao. A rebuilt khazan bund brings back the rice and the prawns, and it holds the water.

voices.title: Neha, Merces
voices.text: Neha teaches by the creek in Merces. Mangroves near the school and the children get to class through the monsoon.

voices.title: Prakash, Mandovi ferry
voices.text: Prakash runs the ferry. The river sits higher at the wharf every year; mangroves along the waterfront would break the surge.

warning.exposed: {place} is exposed! Strengthen it before the {storm}.
warning.lastCall: Last call! {count} homes are still in danger, most of them around {place}.

aftermath.allSaved: Every home in the storm's path is still standing. Panjim is proud of you!
aftermath.someLost: We lost {lost} homes at {place}. A few more defences there next time and they will stand.
aftermath.noDefence: Nothing stood between the {hazard} and {place}. Next time, plant something there first.
